title: A2 Grammar Quiz 3 — Present Perfect, Relative Clauses, Reported Speech (basic)

questions.question: I ___ never ___ sushi.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect = have/has + past participle. 'Eat' → past participle 'eaten'.

questions.question: She ___ already ___ her homework.
questions.explanation: 'She' → 'has'. Past participle of 'finish' → 'finished'. 'Already' goes between have/has and the participle.

questions.question: They ___ to Japan three times.
questions.explanation: 'Have been to' = visited and returned. 'Have gone to' = went and haven't returned yet.

questions.question: Have you done the dishes ___?
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is used in questions and negatives to ask if something has happened before now.

questions.question: I've ___ arrived. I'm still at the airport.
questions.explanation: 'Just' = a very short time ago. It goes between have and the past participle.

questions.question: I ___ him last week.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' is a finished time reference → Past Simple: 'saw'. Present Perfect cannot be used with specific past times.

questions.question: ___ you ever tried Turkish food?
questions.explanation: 'Ever' in questions about life experience → Present Perfect: 'Have you ever...?'

questions.question: She has lived here ___ 2015.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time: 'since 2015', 'since Monday'.

questions.question: I haven't slept ___ three days.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration of time: 'for three days', 'for two years'.

questions.question: He ___ his wallet.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect: 'has' + past participle of 'lose' → 'lost'.

questions.question: The woman ___ lives next door is a nurse.
questions.explanation: 'Who' introduces relative clauses referring to people.

questions.question: This is the car ___ I want to buy.
questions.explanation: 'Which' introduces relative clauses referring to things.

questions.question: That's the boy ___ father is a pilot.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession: 'the boy whose father' = his father.

questions.question: That's the restaurant ___ we had dinner.
questions.explanation: 'Where' introduces relative clauses referring to places.

questions.question: She's the person ___ helped me.
questions.explanation: 'That' can replace 'who' or 'which' in defining relative clauses.

questions.question: He said: 'I am tired.' → He said he ___ tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, Present Simple → Past Simple. 'am' → 'was'.

questions.question: She said: 'I will call you.' → She said she ___ call me.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' → 'would'.

questions.question: He asked: 'Do you like pizza?' → He asked ___ I liked pizza.
questions.explanation: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether': 'asked if I liked...'

questions.question: If it rains, we ___ stay inside.
questions.explanation: First Conditional: If + Present Simple, will + base verb. Real/possible future situation.

questions.question: If she ___ hard, she'll pass the exam.
questions.explanation: In the 'if' clause of First Conditional → Present Simple (not will): 'if she studies'.

questions.question: I'll call you if I ___ any news.
questions.explanation: 'If' clause → Present Simple: 'if I hear'. Main clause → will: 'I'll call'.

questions.question: She speaks very ___. (quick)
questions.explanation: Adverbs modify verbs — add -ly to adjective: 'quick' → 'quickly'.

questions.question: He ___ passed the test. (lucky)
questions.explanation: Adjective 'lucky' ending in -y → change y to i, add -ly: 'luckily'.

questions.question: She runs very ___.
questions.explanation: The adverb form of 'good' is irregular → 'well'. 'Goodly' is not a word.

questions.question: This is ___ bag. (Tom)
questions.explanation: Possessive 's: add apostrophe + s for singular nouns: 'Tom's bag'.

questions.question: The ___ room is messy. (children — plural irregular)
questions.explanation: For irregular plurals (not ending in s), add 's: 'children's room'.

questions.question: It's cold today, ___ it?
questions.explanation: Positive statement → negative tag. 'It is' → 'isn't it?'

questions.question: You don't like spicy food, ___ you?
questions.explanation: Negative statement → positive tag. 'You don't...' → 'do you?'

questions.question: I ___ eaten anything today.
questions.explanation: Negative Present Perfect: 'have/has + not + past participle'. 'haven't eaten'.

questions.question: Have you ___ the news?
questions.explanation: Past participle of 'hear' → 'heard'. Used with Present Perfect: 'have you heard'.
